learn.title: Beyond four sides
learn.body: A polygon is a closed figure made of straight sides. A regular polygon has equal sides and equal angles. There is a simple rule for how the angles add up, whatever the number of sides.

learn.title: Interior angles
learn.body: From one vertex, draw diagonals to split an $n$-sided polygon into $n-2$ triangles. Each triangle gives $180^\circ$, so the interior angles add to $(n-2)\cdot180^\circ$. A regular polygon shares this equally, so each angle is $\frac{(n-2)\cdot180}{n}$.

learn.title: Exterior angles
learn.body: Extend each side and take the angle outside at each vertex. The exterior angles of any polygon add to $360^\circ$. For a regular polygon, each exterior angle is $\frac{360}{n}$, and an interior angle is $180^\circ$ minus it.

learn.title: Work with polygons
steps: Interior angle $150^\circ$ means exterior $30^\circ$, and $360\div30=12$ sides.

learn.body: A quadrilateral gives $(4-2)\cdot180=360^\circ$, the same as before. A triangle gives $180^\circ$. The formula is consistent.
